description: Every relevant Dibbla operation with exactly one state. A capability belongs in /platform only when a stable API backs it, it needs no caller filesystem, keyring, TTY or external binary, and it either finishes promptly or returns a durable pollable ID.

states.summary: Exposed remotely, no side effects. Cannot acknowledge, refresh, rotate or mark-read as a hidden convenience.
Exposed remotely, mutates, uses an idempotency key.
Exposed remotely, requires an accurate destructiveHint, a bound read-only plan and a distinct human approval.
Exposed remotely, returns a durable operation ID that is polled. An MCP call never holds a long run open.
Deliberately never remote. Requires a stated reason.
Intended but not exposed. Requires an owning proposal or API dependency.

capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-534 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset; listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise.

capabilities.title: Update an application's configuration
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-535 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset: the safe configuration update — non-secret environment variables by name (merge, never replace), replicas, cpu and memory within plan; no port, login policy, OAuth scopes or free JSON, and a secret-shaped name or value is refused. Under the same idempotency ledger as restart.

capabilities.title: Restart an application
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-535 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset: rolling restart of an application or one named service, under an idempotency key that deploy-api's durable ledger honours (same key + same request → same answer, no second side effect; changed request → conflict; keys never alias across actor, organization or client). Requires platform:apps:restart; platform:apps:write never substitutes.

capabilities.title: Delete an application
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-536 (P-0035 Part B) as exactly platform_app_delete_plan and platform_app_delete_execute. Plan is read-only and binds the owner/admin OAuth subject, organization, client, grant, exact scope, role, canonical app id/alias, live generation/revision, normalized permanent effects and digest to a random 192-bit request id with a 10-minute TTL. Only the same still-owner/admin human can approve or deny on the CSRF-protected console.<domain>/connector/approvals/<request_id> page; MCP exposes no decision or direct-delete tool. Execute accepts only request_id, revalidates every binding and the live revision under the app lock, atomically redeems server-side approval before one delete/audit row, and durably replays the same terminal result (or IN_PROGRESS) without a second side effect. The request id locates state but never authenticates its holder.

capabilities.title: List deployments
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-537 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset as the deployments family: platform_deployments_list (history from the app's Dibbla-managed main branch, one commit per deploy, plus live status), platform_deployment_get (one revision) and platform_deployment_logs (the current deployment's bounded log window; needs platform:logs:read as well). Read only: no start, no rollback. Listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise.

capabilities.title: Create an agent-authored deployment proposal
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-537 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset as the deployment_proposals family: platform_deployment_proposal_create (a branch in the caller's push namespace, pinned at its head; title and description; an Idempotency-Key that replays to the same proposal; no environment variables, no secret values, no build options) and, under the same scope — the registry defines it as 'create and inspect' — platform_deployment_proposals_list, _get and _events. There is no approve, deny, apply, close or retry tool; the decision stays in the console (P-0034), and a test pins tools/list against one ever appearing.

capabilities.title: Start a deployment
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-671 (P-0035 Part B) and extended by DIB-679, as platform_deployment_start(alias, exactly one of archive{name, content_length, content_sha256} or source{repo, ref}, deploy options, idempotency_key). ONE call owns the whole sequence, from either source; the source is a parameter and never a second tool. With an archive, the call mints the principal-bound upload intent itself and answers with an operation id and the structured upload field a client process pushes the archive to; the deploy starts when the last chunk lands, and an interrupted upload resumes against the same intent without creating a second deploy. With repo and ref, no bytes move at all: the application may only name the repository it is already linked to, the ref is pinned to a commit sha by the call, and the platform fetches that commit itself with its own credential — which is what makes the path work from a cloud sandbox whose network reaches the provider's MCP servers and GitHub but not this origin. No credential, token or byte reaches MCP, model context, logs or audit on either path. A ref that does not exist, a repository the application is not linked to and a repository in another tenant are ONE absence answer. The build never holds the MCP call open; the generic operation tools expose status, bounded build logs, events, output (the app's URL on success, the CLI's own build error on failure) and cancel. Organization deployment governance is obeyed, not bypassed: immediate rolls out, while admin_four_eyes, member_four_eyes and admin_checkpoint instead create a pending deploy whose effective model and console decision path are named in the output, and whose console page shows the repository, ref and commit sha behind a git-sourced candidate. There is no approve, deny, apply, close or retry tool — CanDecide in deploy-api refuses the author regardless of role, and a test pins tools/list against one ever appearing.

capabilities.title: Read a bounded application log window
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-534 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset; listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise.

capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-538 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset; listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise. A secret value is never returned by any tool. A set on an existing name rotates it; routine write with an idempotency key.

capabilities.title: Delete a secret
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-538 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset. Routine write with an idempotency key under the same write scope P-0035 assigns to set/rotate/delete; not remote-destructive, because there is no secrets destructive scope and the proposal's plan/confirm flow is for app, database and storage deletion.

capabilities.title: List managed databases
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_databases_list with cursor pagination. Returns only organization-owned name, PostgreSQL version, linked app, creation time, size, table count and phase; never DSN, host, user, password or secret material.

capabilities.title: Inspect bounded database metadata
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_get. Returns the same explicit metadata allowlist as list after organization ownership validation; no schema, row data or credentials.

capabilities.title: Read database lifecycle status
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_status. Returns provisioning, ready, restoring or failed with only the bounded database metadata allowlist.

capabilities.title: Run a bounded structured read-only SELECT
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_rows_query and intentionally absent from tools/list under metadata-only platform:databases:read. The caller supplies one database, one public base table, explicit catalog-validated columns, typed eq|in|lt|lte|gt|gte|is_null filters, at most one order_by, cursor and limit — never SQL, schema, join, view, CTE, function, expression, offset or wildcard. The server builds one parametrized SELECT with a SELECT-only role and read-only transaction, and enforces 100 rows, two seconds and 256 KiB. Audit stores actor and shape but never filter or cell values.

capabilities.title: Provision a managed database
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_provision(name, app_alias?, idempotency_key). Returns a durable database_provision operation immediately; identical normalized retries replay it and changed payloads conflict. Deploy-api persists, leases and resumes the work, while the generic operation tools expose status, events, logs, output and cancel.

capabilities.title: Restore a database from a backup
capabilities.note: Reclassified from remote-async to remote-destructive by DIB-673 (P-0035 Part F) and rebuilt as platform_database_restore_plan and platform_database_restore_execute; the direct platform_database_restore tool and its deploy-api route are gone, because a second way in would be a way around the confirmation. The reason is what restore does, not what it is called: loading a dump into a database that already exists drops and recreates every object the dump defines, so the data held today is replaced and Dibbla cannot bring it back — the same semantics as `dibbla db restore`, which is the parity this row satisfies. The plan is read-only and names the database, how many tables and bytes are about to be overwritten, and the source file by opaque source_file_id — never a transfer id, hash, ticket, session or bytes — or states plainly that nothing is overwritten when the target does not exist yet. A human approves on the same CSRF-protected console page as every other destructive capability. Execute accepts only request_id, re-reads database and source and refuses either having changed, and returns a durable operation immediately because a large dump outlives one call; the operation records the confirmation it was redeemed under, and the confirmation records the operation, so the audit reads in both directions. The confirmation, not an idempotency key, is what makes one approved intent produce one restore.

capabilities.title: Delete a managed database
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-673 (P-0035 Part F) as exactly platform_database_delete_plan and platform_database_delete_execute, on the same machinery as app and bucket deletion and with no shortcut of its own. Plan is read-only and binds the owner/admin OAuth subject, organization, client, grant, exact scope, role, the canonical database identity and a digest of its live metadata — size, table count, bound application — to a random request id with a 10-minute TTL, and enumerates what disappears: every table and byte, the dedicated PostgreSQL role and its credentials, the ownership record, the injected DATABASE_URL_<NAME> secret and the application left without a database. Only the same still-owner/admin human decides on the CSRF-protected console.<domain>/connector/approvals/<request_id> page; MCP exposes no decision and no direct delete. Execute accepts only request_id, re-reads the live metadata and refuses a database that changed after planning, atomically claims the approval before the single drop, and durably replays the same terminal result. A database in another organization is absent in both directions, because ownership — not the request — resolves the name.

capabilities.title: List object-storage buckets
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-541 (P-0035 Part B / P-0026) as platform_storage_buckets_list and platform_storage_bucket_get. Both return only tenant-owned bucket name, quota, used bytes, object count, optional deployment, four secret names, creation time and status; credentials, endpoints, MinIO details, policies and object contents cannot enter the response. Platform and connector buckets are absent from this surface.

capabilities.title: Create a bucket with scoped credentials
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-541 (P-0035 Part B / P-0026) as synchronous platform_storage_bucket_provision. A required idempotency key binds the actor, organization, client, target and payload; exact retry replays, changed payload conflicts. The control plane creates the hard quota, lifecycle rule, bucket-scoped service account and four STORAGE_<NAME>_* secrets atomically from the caller's perspective, and never returns credential material.

capabilities.title: Rotate bucket credentials
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-541 (P-0035 Part B / P-0026) as synchronous, idempotent platform_storage_bucket_rotate under the narrow rotate scope. The old credential is invalidated, the two credential secrets are replaced and every service in a bound deployment must accept a restart before success; there is no no_restart input. Organization-global buckets report that restart is not applicable. Credential material is never returned.

capabilities.title: Delete a bucket
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-541 (P-0035 Part B / P-0026) as exactly platform_storage_bucket_delete_plan and platform_storage_bucket_delete_execute. The 10-minute random request binds owner/admin subject, organization, client, grant, role, exact scope, bucket identity, current credential-free metadata, normalized force-delete effects and digest. Only the same authenticated human approves in the CSRF-protected console; MCP has no decision, direct-delete or force tool. Execute accepts only request_id, revalidates metadata, atomically claims once, then force-deletes all objects, bucket, service account, ownership and four secrets while concurrent/retried calls receive IN_PROGRESS or the same terminal result. Platform and connector buckets never enter this surface.

capabilities.title: List workflows and revisions
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-539 (P-0035 Part B2) on mcp-server's /platform toolset as platform_workflows_list, platform_workflow_get, platform_workflow_revisions, platform_workflow_tools and platform_workflow_validate (validate saves nothing). Read through core's slim API under the verified principal; a workflow in another organization is NOT_FOUND.

capabilities.title: Create or replace a workflow definition in one call
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-674 (P-0035 Part F) as exactly ONE tool, platform_workflow_apply(name, definition, idempotency_key). The whole editing surface is a desired state, not graph mutations: the definition is the COMPLETE workflow in the same slim YAML `dibbla wf` reads, and the stored workflow becomes equal to it — what the definition omits is removed. A family of node, edge, input and wiring tools was deliberately NOT built; the desired state is what makes the change atomic and idempotent by construction, validates the whole graph as one document instead of one mutation at a time, and grows the connector by one tool instead of six. The name in the path is the only name that decides which workflow is written; the one in the document is ignored. The whole graph is validated before anything is saved, so a cycle, a dangling edge, a missing input or an unknown node type refuses the apply with findings that name the location in the definition and leaves no partly saved workflow. A required idempotency key binds actor, organization, client, target and definition through deploy-api's durable ledger: the exact retry replays the first answer and creates no second revision, a changed definition under the same key conflicts. Every apply leaves a revision holding the state it replaced (on a create, the workflow as created), which is what platform.workflows.restore returns to. The answer says what the change did — added, changed, removed — by the author's own step labels and connections, never by internal ids, and never by quoting a field's value back. A definition references credentials and data sources by name; one carrying the engine's reserved per-run _credentials map is refused before any request leaves the connector, so no credential value can reach a stored graph through MCP or model context. A workflow in another organization is absent in both directions, and the result is runnable through the existing platform_workflow_execute path.

capabilities.title: Return a workflow to an earlier revision
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-674 (P-0035 Part F) as platform_workflow_restore(name, revision, idempotency_key), the second and last tool this capability adds. Revisions are the history of applies rather than a separate editing model: platform_workflow_revisions lists them and this puts one back as HEAD. A restore snapshots what it replaces before it runs, so it is itself reversible, and it carries the same required idempotency key as an apply. HEAD is refused as a revision id — restoring HEAD onto HEAD is not a thing a caller means. A workflow or revision in another organization answers the same absence a name that never existed answers.

capabilities.title: Execute a workflow at a pinned immutable revision
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-539 (P-0035 Part B2/B3) as platform_workflow_execute: starts the run at HEAD asynchronously with a required idempotency_key (same key + same request replays the run, a different request under the same key is IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT) and returns the durable operation envelope wrapping the canonical run id. Pinning a named immutable revision is a later addition.

capabilities.title: Prepare a principal-bound download of a file or an app's own source
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-543 (P-0035 Part B4) as platform_file_download_prepare plus platform_file_transfer_status; DIB-672 (Part F) adds an agent-redeemed second path over the same machinery and a second origin. Prepare accepts EITHER an opaque source_file_id OR an application alias with an optional revision — never both, never a byte or base64 field — and returns a principal-bound intent with safe metadata, the authenticated fallback link and, for a grant that can read, a principal-bound download URL on this resource's own origin. The application origin is the parity with `dibbla clone`: deploy-api cuts a gzipped tar of that app's Dibbla-managed repository at the named or latest deployed revision, bounded by the same archive limit a deploy obeys, ingests it into the DIB-542 broker under the caller's own binding and mints an ordinary download over the opaque file identity that comes back, so the intent declares the exact content_length and content_sha256 before a byte moves. An app in another organization, an app the caller cannot reach, an installation with version control off and a revision that does not exist are one answer: absent. That URL is never a presigned storage URL and the term is not a synonym for one: it is principal-bound, the caller authenticates, and no storage host is named. Who redeems the one-time ticket is the only difference between the two paths. Browser-mediated: the same authenticated human opens console.<domain>/connector/transfers/<transfer_id>, the server redeems the ticket outside model context and gives only that browser the Dibbla-Transfer session. Agent-redeemed: the client process GETs <resource-origin>/platform/v1/file-transfers/<transfer_id>/bytes with its own platform access token for the same grant; the first range redeems the ticket server-side and the server serves a bounded window, answering 206 with the window it served. A resume names the byte the CLIENT actually reached: only the receiver knows how much of an interrupted range it kept, so any range inside the file is served for as long as the intent lives, and the recorded offset is a high-water mark rather than a cursor a caller must match. Both paths share one transfer_id, one intent ledger and the uncached live-grant check that stops the next range after a revoke. Ticket/session plaintext, broker credentials, presigned storage URLs and file bytes are absent from the durable intent ledger, MCP results, model context, logs and audit; audit keeps correlation id, principal and operation.

capabilities.title: Prepare a principal-bound resumable browser upload
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-543 (P-0035 Part B4) as platform_file_upload_prepare plus platform_file_transfer_abort; DIB-670 (Part F) adds an agent-redeemed second path over the same machinery. Direction-bound platform_file_transfer_status requires platform:files:write for the caller's own upload and platform:files:read for a download; download prepare always requires platform:files:read. Prepare accepts only name, content_type, exact content_length, content_sha256 and idempotency_key—never a byte/base64 field—and returns a principal-bound intent with safe metadata, the authenticated fallback link and, for a grant that can write, a principal-bound upload URL on this resource's own origin. That URL is never a presigned storage URL and the term is not a synonym for one: it is principal-bound, and the caller authenticates. Who redeems the one-time ticket is the only difference between the two paths. Browser-mediated: the authenticated human opens the console page, whose browser verifies every declared field, redeems the encrypted ticket outside model context and uploads chunks with Dibbla-Transfer. Agent-redeemed: the client process PUTs bounded chunks to <resource-origin>/platform/v1/file-transfers/<transfer_id>/bytes with Upload-Offset, authenticating with its own platform access token for the same grant; the first chunk redeems the ticket server-side. The URL carries no signature, ticket or session—it locates one transfer and the token decides—so a redeemed, expired or foreign-principal redemption is refused as absent, and it is a structured field the client acts on rather than prose the model repeats. Both paths share one transfer_id, one intent ledger, one resume offset and the uncached live-grant check that stops the next chunk after a revoke. Declared length or sha256 that does not hold ends the intent and produces no file. Completion publishes only the opaque source_file_id back to MCP. Abort is idempotent and never deletes a completed file. Ticket/session plaintext, presigned storage URLs and bytes are absent from the durable intent ledger, MCP results, model context, logs and audit.

capabilities.title: Delete a file
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-673 (P-0035 Part F) as exactly platform_file_delete_plan and platform_file_delete_execute. A file is named by its opaque source_file_id and never by a content hash, transfer id, ticket or session: the content hash is a dedup key shared across organizations, so it is not an identity. Plan is read-only, quotes name, size, content hash and status, and says what stops working — every capability that names the file, including database restore and file download — while stating that the content-addressed blob is deliberately left in place because it is shared with every other record holding the same bytes. The approval boundary is deploy-api's one confirmation ledger even though the records live in the broker, so there is a single audit to read and a single shape to review. Execute accepts only request_id, refuses a file renamed or replaced after planning, is single-use, durably replays its terminal result, and answers absent for another organization in both directions. No byte, object key or storage host can appear on this surface.

capabilities.title: Poll a durable operation by its principal-bound ID
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-539 (P-0035 Part B3) as platform_operation_status, platform_operation_events, platform_operation_logs and platform_operation_output; extended by DIB-540 to database-operation IDs. Typed phase and cursor-paged content come from the resource's durable engine. The operation id is data, never authentication; an operation in another organization is NOT_FOUND.

capabilities.title: Cancel a durable operation
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-539 (P-0035 Part B3) as platform_operation_cancel and extended by DIB-540 to database-operation IDs: idempotent, valid only while cancellable, CONFLICT once finished; a terminal state is never rewritten.

capabilities.title: Archive a local repository for deploy
capabilities.reason: Reads the caller's filesystem and builds the upload archive.

capabilities.title: Validate dibbla.yaml offline
capabilities.reason: Validates a file on the caller's disk with no platform round-trip.

capabilities.title: Run a dibbla-task.yaml pipeline
capabilities.reason: Executes commands on the caller's machine.

capabilities.title: Switch the local CLI context
capabilities.reason: Local state, and a model-controlled context switch is forbidden outright: the connector URL selects the installation and the OAuth grant selects user and org.

capabilities.title: Authenticate the CLI and store credentials
capabilities.reason: Uses the OS keyring and a TTY.

capabilities.title: Update the CLI binary in place
capabilities.reason: Replaces a binary on the caller's machine.
